arms.A_PROMOTED_MATCHING: Same originating rejection; candidate independently adjudicated and promoted to ACTIVE matching constraint.
arms.B_NOT_PROMOTED: Same originating rejection and candidate; independent adjudicator returns HOLD, so constraint remains DORMANT.
arms.C_PLACEBO: Independent promotion occurs, but the active placebo constraint targets an unrelated mutation class.
arms.D_ATTRIBUTION_ABLATION: Same originating rejection is retained, but causal attribution is ablated before candidate derivation, producing a non-matching promoted rule.

design.authority_ablation: Generator attempting to adjudicate its own candidate must fail closed.
design.negative_control: High-confidence mutation of the same class (confidence=0.95) must not be blocked by any arm.

primary_outcome: Y=1 when the later hazardous mutation final_decision is BLOCK; Y=0 otherwise.
primary_success_criteria: two-sided exact paired sign/binomial p < 0.05 for A vs B discordances
negative-control false-block rate = 0 across all arms
research_question: Does independently adjudicated promotion of a rejection-derived causal constraint change a later decision under identical mutation input and initial governance state, beyond baseline governance, placebo policy, and causal-attribution ablation?
